scope: Independent source review of the exact 13 frozen 18–24-month toddler-practical-home placements, their full reading surfaces and all assigned opening/topic summaries. Separate actual-image art-context review for pouring and shoes; the other eleven placements have null art contexts. No publication determination or review of unassigned entries.
independence: This reviewer independently read the original PDF page text and full-page visual material. Research/author records were not used as substitutes for source reading. Other source/tone review files were not inspected. The draft, app, sources, artwork, shared documentation and LEARNINGS files were not edited.

textPlacement.assessment: The opening title/action label/invitation and cue retain a small manageable jug, little water, interest and nearby help. Both topic rows independently retain manageability, a cloth and help. The full entry preserves slow showing, partial repetition and shared wiping; its three adult-and-child steps do not demand a full child work cycle. The exact 12–18-month chart example and 18+ appendix label are both visible, with the chart retaining earlier activities. The references support this ordinary pouring invitation; it adds no drinking quantity, equipment dimension, mandatory grip or independent-care standard.

artContext.assessment: Pass for this exact pouring text/art binding. The actual image shows a standing toddler at a low table pouring from a small pitcher into a cup; one hand holds the pitcher and the other steadies the cup. A caregiver is kneeling close by and a cloth is on the table. The public text requires a manageable jug and nearby help but does not prescribe two hands on the pitcher. The scene, title, invitation and observation cue fit the source’s ordinary small-jug invitation without adding a grip lesson or a claim of independent care. The shared shelf background and corrected bottom-tier shoe-basket alt are accurate.

issues.finding: The original appendix p.250 labels Handwashing at table as 18+ months (able to carry a jug), and its description specifies a child wanting to repeat handwashing at the sink. The frozen copy retains 18+ and repetition but omits the jug-carrying condition from all public surfaces. The sink variant has a different 14+ row and should remain distinct.
issues.requiredCorrection: Restore the table-specific jug-carrying readiness beside the 18+ label and in the table description/reference locator. For example: the book’s separate table is for a child who wants to repeat sink handwashing and can carry a jug. Keep ordinary shared sink washing and its 14+ source label separate; do not add a handwashing protocol or equipment specification.

textPlacement.assessment: The short topic row is an accurate attributed perspective on shared care and does not promise independent handwashing. The sink materials, partial care and separate-table distinction are otherwise supported. However, the full entry’s table description, numerical age context and reference locator omit the table row’s additional ability-to-carry-a-jug condition. A general offer of adult help does not preserve that specific source readiness label; revise the identified surfaces before this text component can pass.
